title: E2EMap: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for CGRA Compilation via Reverse Mapping
problem: CGRA mappers using heuristics or combinatorial optimization cannot learn from past experience and suffer from poor quality and portability. Previous hybrid approaches mixing ML with heuristics remain suboptimal because they only address partial components of the mapping process.
motivation: CGRAs are promising for high performance and energy efficiency, but actual performance depends critically on mapper quality, making improvements in mapping algorithms essential.
method: The tool uses policy gradient reinforcement learning—machine learning through trial and error—to compile code for CGRAs (specialized reconfigurable chips) by learning the entire process as one problem rather than separate steps. It employs reverse mapping, which analyzes hardware constraints backwards to determine which instructions can fit where and how to route them, making the learning problem simpler while exploring many routing options. This end-to-end approach learns the complete compilation pipeline without relying on hand-written rules.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using reinforcement learning with reverse mapping to learn CGRA compilation end-to-end as a unified optimization problem, rather than decomposing it with separate hand-written rules.
contributions: End-to-end learning framework covering the full CGRA mapping process
Reverse mapping problem formulation to reduce model complexity and exploration space
Policy gradient reinforcement learning approach for learning from scratch
Achieves 2.23x mapping quality improvement with reduced compilation time
limitations: Evaluation scope, scalability to larger CGRAs, and applicability across diverse CGRA architectures not discussed.
